metadata.name: Grayhaven
metadata.subtitle: Town, coast and countryside
metadata.description: Explore the streets, quays, farmsteads, orchards and fields of Grayhaven. Building functions, district names and stories are fictional interpretations of the map artwork.
metadata.credit: Fantasy map generated from a user-supplied Google Maps screenshot and styled with the Dragonsgate map as a visual reference. Original map data © Google. Buildings and stories are fictional.

landmarks.name: Crown Monument
landmarks.description: A freestanding monument at the center of Crown Square. The name and civic role are fictional.

landmarks.name: Hall of the West Wind
landmarks.description: A column-fronted hall beside Crossing Way, overlooking the western farms.

landmarks.name: Westhaven Court House
landmarks.description: A square courtyard building beside the western road. Residents use it as their local meeting house.

landmarks.name: Garden Grange
landmarks.description: The long north range of a walled farmstead surrounding a planted courtyard.

landmarks.name: North Croft Hall
landmarks.description: A long hall among the north-coast crofts, used by the local growers guild.

landmarks.name: Temple of the Tides
landmarks.description: A large roofed hall near the eastern waterfront. Its religious use is part of Grayhaven’s fictional setting.

landmarks.name: East Ward Court
landmarks.description: An elongated civic hall within the eastern town blocks.

landmarks.name: Diamond Guildhall
landmarks.description: A ridge-roofed hall beside the lower town approaches, assigned as the ward’s guild meeting place.

landmarks.name: South Grange
landmarks.description: The eastern range of a large farm court near the southern crossing.

landmarks.name: Long Quay Warehouse
landmarks.description: A long waterfront building used as a cooperage and warehouse in the fictional town.

landmarks.name: West Farm Barn
landmarks.description: A long barn beside the curving West Farm Road.

landmarks.name: Southwest Longhouse
landmarks.description: A long roadside building serving travelers on the southwestern approach.
